What's new in 2.29.0

One new tool: Agent Watch, which keeps an eye on the Claude Code sessions you have running so you don't have to sit and watch them — and gives each one a character you'll come to recognise.

Agent Watch ⌃⌥M

  • Every session you have running, in one panel. The project, the last thing the agent said, and what it's doing right now — the ones wanting your attention first. Type to search by project or title.
  • A character for every session. Twenty-one little pixel animals, one per project, and never the same one twice on screen. They walk while an agent is working, shuffle about when one wants an answer, and stand still when it's done — so you can read a whole panel of them without reading a word. Click any of them in Settings to meet it.
  • Status at a glance. A green light for working, yellow for a session that needs you, grey for one at rest, with the state in words and how long it's been that way counting up beside it.
  • It taps you on the shoulder. A notification when a turn finishes, and when a session has been sitting on a permission prompt long enough that it's clearly waiting for you. Optionally in plain language, summarised on-device by Apple Intelligence.
  • Answer without leaving what you're doing. Type a reply straight into the notification and Dax puts it in the exact terminal tab that asked — Terminal, iTerm, or Ghostty. If it can't find the tab for certain, it says so and leaves your answer on the clipboard rather than typing it somewhere else.
  • Click to go to it. The whole card is the button. Dax finds the tab running that session and brings it to the front, following it to another Desktop if that's where it lives.
  • Close the terminal and the session leaves the list. What's listed is what's running — Dax checks for the agent process itself rather than trusting a file that outlives the session that wrote it.
  • Hooks, if you want them. Claude Code can tell Dax outright when it needs you instead of Dax working it out from the trace. Two entries in ~/.claude/settings.json, added and removed from Settings, backed up first.
  • All of it on your Mac. Agent Watch reads the session files already on disk and never touches the network.

Also in this release

  • Open Project's toast now shows what you actually opened. The agent's own logo when you started Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, or Gemini, and a folder when you opened a folder — instead of the same window icon for everything.
  • Signed, notarized, universal (Apple Silicon & Intel), macOS 14+.
